summary: Camp is closing. The quarterback is settled, the left tackle is not, and the defense left the second scrimmage with four takeaways.

items.headline: Sarkisian is not worried about Arch Manning
items.tldr: The offense turned it over four times in 120 scrimmage plays and Sarkisian still called it a great camp for Manning, pointing at his timing with Ryan Wingo, Cam Coleman and Emmett Mosley. The quarterback is not the open question here; the ten around him are.

items.headline: The ruling that sidelined others does not reach Cole Hutson
items.tldr: A federal appeals court froze the order letting 2022-class athletes return for a fifth year, but Hutson's came from his own settlement with the NCAA, so it holds. Texas keeps a lineman with 23 career starts at guard and center in the month its front is thinnest.

items.headline: The defense won the second scrimmage
items.tldr: Four takeaways, one of them a Kosi Okpala pick-six, against an offense Sarkisian called too sloppy. Mosley caught two touchdowns anyway. If that split is real and not just August, early downs against Texas State will show it first.

items.headline: Goosby's knee is a bone bruise, with no return date announced
items.tldr: ESPN reported the left tackle's injury as a bone bruise, and no timetable had been set. That keeps left tackle as Texas' clearest open question before Texas State.

items.headline: The edge rotation runs deeper than Colin Simmons
items.tldr: Lance Jackson, Colton Vasek and five-star freshman Richard Wesley are all in the mix behind Simmons. If that depth holds, Texas can keep rotating without asking Simmons to carry every pass-rush snap into the fourth quarter.
